Same group: the scope a security analysis states versus the attacker it assumes. Threat Models owns assets, goals, assumptions and exclusions; Adversaries owns capabilities, resources and corruption.
Same group: two shapes of the decomposition the parent already states. Split by what each rules out or requires and how each is established.
Same group; the Security prose says availability is not liveness. Availability protects the service and its data; liveness is the eventual-progress shape any property can take.

facetWatch.note: Checking instead of trusting, checking a computation, and checking code against a specification. One exposition only at the level of checking conformance to a stated claim by evidence.
Preferred placement under Derivatives is the narrowest context; the exposition must be general.
Every placement means handing a decision upward; the title invites a privilege-escalation reading.

Four placements. Central meaning: deliberate coordination among distinct parties pursuing an aligned outcome through explicit or covert agreement; say when it undermines protocol rules, market integrity or other participants without implying every instance is illegal or prohibited. Name, never explain: Sybil identities (one party, many identities), Coalition Formation, Bribery, and Algorithmic Collusion (tacit convergence without agreement, already explained by the Market Power parent). Trust Distribution owns counting colluders against thresholds.

Four placements; two parents already state its core, and Fault Models owns fault classes and thresholds. Go beyond them: masking, fail-safe and non-masking tolerance (which properties survive, which recover), correlated failures, tolerance versus recovery. Redundancy, Graceful Degradation, Failure Isolation, Recovery and Automatic Failover are named only.

The parent already lists agreement, conventions, markets and a designated coordinator. Go beyond the list: what each assumes about information, incentives and enforcement, and when each fails. Consensus, Markets and Coordination Mechanisms are named only.

Coordinating sense: how information relevant to coordination is distributed, accessible and verifiable (private or public, symmetric or not), and how that structure shapes expectations and choices. Partial Knowledge owns what processes can know or infer under communication and observation limits, layered knowledge included: name it, never re-explain it.

The parent already defines the coordinating sense. Go beyond it: when signals change expectations without binding anyone, and what makes them credible. Communication owns message delivery; Commitment Devices owns binding commitments.

Two placements: the free-rider problem (Foundations) and several parties pursuing related outcomes (Intents, whose parent already explains conditional pledges). One meaning: joint action toward a shared outcome and the incentive problem it faces. Coordination Mechanisms, Commitment Devices and Coordination Failures are named only; Collective Action is not Guaranteed Cooperation.

The statement that scopes a security analysis: protected assets, attacker capabilities and goals, assumptions and exclusions, and how it bounds what a guarantee claims. Threat Modeling owns the analysis activity (attack trees, payoffs, keeping it current); Security Assumptions and Trust Assumptions own the assumptions themselves. Name them, never explain them.

The attacker: what it can observe, delay, inject or corrupt, the scarce resources that bound it rather than identities (the parent already says so), static versus adaptive corruption, and its operational limits. Byzantine Behavior owns what a corrupted participant does.

Domain prose already defines it, and Fault Models owns fault classes and thresholds such as more than three times as many processes as faults. Go beyond: what it can do that a crash cannot (equivocation, selective omission, false claims about others) and what makes it detectable or attributable. Strategic Behavior owns rational deviation.

Exclusion of particular actions or participants by whoever controls inclusion or access (proposers, sequencers, relays, interfaces, network operators) through omission, delay or filtering; omission is hard to tell apart from congestion. Censorship Resistance owns the defenses: name it only.

Two placements; the parent already gives the decomposition and the finality and halting examples. Go beyond: a violation shows in a finite prefix and cannot be undone, invariant-style arguments, and why partially synchronous consensus keeps safety whatever the timing. The decomposition covers properties of individual executions only, which confidentiality is not. Formal Specifications owns how properties are written; Invariants is named only.

Two placements; the parent already gives the decomposition. Go beyond: no finite prefix rules it out, progress arguments, and the fairness and timing assumptions it needs, such as progress only once the network stabilizes. Same individual-execution scope as Safety.

Two placements: the service and its data remain obtainable when requested. Not Liveness, not Censorship Resistance (each valid action) and not Data Availability (publication of data). Distinguish the partition sense the parent uses (every non-failed replica answers) from uptime measures. Denial-of-Service Attacks and Redundancy are named only.

Replica sense fixed by the domain prose: what different participants may observe of the same state; not the ACID sense of integrity constraints. Compare models by strength only as far as the claims need. State Machine Replication owns how replicas apply one sequence; Finality and Agreement are named only.
Five placements across governance, security, execution, autonomous protocols and economic resilience.
Five placements; parent sentences about pausing exist in several of them.
Governance, organizational and machine constitutions as facets of one meaning.
Capability-based authority throughout; not model capabilities.
